Subject Illegal functioning by the Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei
Tax Bureau.
Made by D. I. Hutton Forwarded by

Sir:
At 4.05 p.m. 18/1/39 a telephone message was received informing the station of Japanese from the Kiangsu, Chekiang & Anhwei Tax Bureau again visiting 177 Yangchow Road.
The undersigned accompanied by D.S. Smita and J.P.S. 9 proceeded to the scene and found the 2 Japanese who were formerly handed over to Mr. Maeda and Mr. Maeda himself on the premises of the wine shop.
J.P.S. 9 was requested to inquire the business of the Japanese and the answer was given as "They wished to buy wine" and had a right to be in the shop. The Police remained on the premises but no attempt was made to buy wine. The 3 Japanese were again asked regarding their business and replied they wished to know the price of the wine. No attempt was made by either to ask the shop assistants the price of wine and from inquiries in the vicinity it was ascertained that when the 3 Japanese arrived in car 8077 they asked for the shopmaster and asked several people in the vicinity if they were Chinese detectives. The shop proprietor on arrival of the Police was absent from the shop. Mr. Maeda took exception to the undersigned's presence and commenced to use abusive language (in Japanese). Mr. Maeda was requested to give his name through the interpretation of J.P.S. 9 but refused to do so and proceeded behind the shop counter to a telephone installed by the shop owner. Mr. Maeda telephoned to J.D.S. 149 and requested his presence at the wine shop as the undersigned was interfering with him and he thought he may be taken to the station.
On arrival of J.D.S. 149 Urakami Mr. Maeda was requested

日期：1939 年 1 月 18 日

制作人：侦探督察赫顿 (D. I. Hutton) 转发人

先生：
1939 年 1 月 18 日下午 4 点 05 分，接到电话消息，通知捕房来自江苏、浙江、安徽税务局的日本人再次访问扬州路 177 号。
署名人与特别调查员斯米塔 (D.S. Smita) 及日捕巡长 9 号 (J.P.S. 9) 一同前往现场，发现之前移交给前田先生 (Mr. Maeda) 的两名日本人以及前田先生本人正在那家酒铺内。
要求日捕巡长 9 号询问日本人的来意，回答是“他们想买酒”，并有权待在店里。警察留在店内，但无人尝试买酒。再次询问这三名日本人的来意，他们回答说想知道酒的价格。双方均未向店员询问酒价，经向附近打听，查明这三名日本人乘坐 8077 号汽车到达时，曾寻找店主，并询问附近的几个人是否是中国侦探。警察到达时，店主不在店内。前田先生对署名人在场表示异议，并开始使用辱骂性语言（日语）。通过日捕巡长 9 号的翻译，要求前田先生出示姓名，但他拒绝这样做，并走到店柜台后面使用店主安装的电话。前田先生致电日捕探员 149 号 (J.D.S. 149)，要求他到酒铺来，因为署名人正在干涉他，他认为自己可能会被带到捕房。
日捕探员 149 号浦上 (Urakami) 到达后，要求前田先生

经在附近查访，当地中国居民认为日本人意图将店主带走，并已通知警署。

经查，所用机动车（牌照号 8077）登记在刘罗斯玛丽（Rose Marie Liu）小姐名下，地址为迈杰斯蒂克公寓（Majestic Apartments）116 号。值得注意的是，首次将日本人和中国人带至警署时所用车辆（牌照号 1542）的司机，此前曾受雇于迈杰斯蒂克公寓 116 号的刘罗斯玛丽小姐。

随即致电该地址查询机动车 8077 的情况，核实确认该车仍属登记车主所有。但车主表示她不知晓该车被用于榆林路区域，但会进行查询。

先生，

遵照警务助理处长致犯罪科侦探长的指示，因涉及非法活动及企图勒索而被中央警署拘留的中国男子葉智化（Yih Tseu Hoo），其在江苏浙江安徽税务局任职期间涉案，已于1939年1月18日获释，其由该局签发的委任证已归还。

Made by D.I. Hutton. Forwarded by____

Sir,

Further to the reports of illegal functioning of the Kiangsu
Chekiang and Anhwei Tax Bureau, the Chinese arrested and detained
at Central Station in accordance with the instructions of the
Commissioner of Police was interviewed by the undersigned on
15-1-39 and the following information was obtained. The detained
man admitted having operated in Yulin Road Area on previous
occasions and mentioned the following shops where he had visited.

(1) Yuen Tsang Siang (源昌祥) Wire Shop, 216 Yenshan Road.
(2) Nyeu Shing (元興) Wine Shop 836 Any Road.
(3) Soong Tsung Lee (松春義) Wine & Sauce Shop, 90 Thorburn Rd.
(4) Tsang Tong Shing (張宗新) Wine & Sauce Shop, 700 Seoul Road (Yangtsepoo District)

Enquiries were made by U.J.S. 104 and the shops mentioned by
the detained man and the following information was obtained:-

(1) The Chinese known as Yih (葉) accompanied by Japanese
visited the shop on several occasions and demanded that the
proprietor pay tax to the Kiangsu Chekiang and Anhwei Tax
Bureau failing which they would close his shop, arrest the
proprietor and hand him over to the Japanese Military Police.
The proprietor being scared eventually paid $65.00 ($50.00 for
a fine and $15.00 ricsha money) a receipt was given for $50
in the name of the Tax Bureau.

(2) The Chinese known as Yih accompanied by the Japanese visit
ed the shop on several occasions and demanded that the proprie
-tor pay taxes to the Kiangsu Chekiang and Anhwei Tax Bureau
failing which they would close his shop, arrest him and hand
him over to the Japanese Military Police. Eventually the pro-
prietor paid $15.00 tax.

先生，

继有关江苏浙江安徽税务局非法活动的报告之后，根据警察总监的指示，在中央警署被捕并拘留的中国人于1939年1月15日由具名人进行了问询，并获得如下信息。被拘留者承认此前曾在榆林路区域活动，并提及了他曾光顾的以下店铺。

(1) 源昌祥五金店，延山路 216 号。
(2) 元興酒行，安远路（Any Road） 836 号。
(3) 松春義酱园，韬朋路（Thorburn Rd.） 90 号。
(4) 張宗新酱园，首尔路（Seoul Road）（杨树浦区） 700 号

由日籍巡捕 U.J.S. 104 对被拘留者提及的店铺进行了查询，获得如下信息：-

(1) 被称为葉（Yih）的中国人陪同日本人多次光顾该店，要求店主向江苏浙江安徽税务局缴纳税款，否则将关闭其店铺，逮捕店主并将其移交给日本宪兵队。店主因恐惧最终支付了 65.00 美元（其中 50.00 美元为罚款，15.00 美元为黄包车费），并收到了一张以税务局名义开具的 50 美元收据。

(2) 被称为葉的中国人陪同日本人多次光顾该店，要求店主向江苏浙江安徽税务局缴纳税款，否则将关闭其店铺，逮捕他并将其移交给日本宪兵队。最终店主支付了 15.00 美元税款。

Sir:

As mentioned in the last paragraph of Y.R. Misc. 6/39,
detectives were detailed to keep observation on the wine shop
occupied by Woo Ying Daung at 177 Yangchow Road.

At 4 p.m. 13/1/39 M/car 1542 driven by a male Chinese and
3 passengers (2 Japanese and 1 Chinese) arrived and stopped in
front of complt's shop. The Chinese immediately asked the owner
why he had failed to send money to the "Tax Bureau" and when the
owner stated he had no money the Chinese accompanied by the 2
Japanese entered the shop and informed the owner to proceed to
the godown which is a Chinese house situated across the alleyway
from the rear door of the shop, House No. 3 lane 122 Thorburn Road
where they would seal 12 jars of wine as he had failed to pay.
The value of the 12 jars of wine is $250.00.

C.D.C. 220 one of the 4 detectives posted on duty immediately
communicated with the station and the undersigned accompanied by
D. C. Smith, S. I. Davies and J.P.C. 71 attended.

Upon arrival at the shop the chauffeur was detained and on
entering House 3 Lane 122 Thorburn Road 2 Japanese and 1 Chinese
were observed sealing complt's wine jars with seals which when
translated read as follows:-

"Kiangying Wine Shop. Sealed by Kiangsu Provincial Tax
Bureau for Rolled Tobacco and Wine. Dated 12/1/39 and chopped
by Kiangsu Provincial Tax Bureau for Rolled Tobacco and Wine"
(One seal attached to the original report).

Upon being informed that the undersigned was a representative
of the S.M.P. and that they had no authority to seal complt's
property or to tax and fine him they replied that they were from
the Tax Bureau and were sent to seal complt's property. The 3 men

先生：

正如榆林路杂项档案 6/39 最后一段所述，已指派侦探对吴英堂（Woo Ying Daung，音译）占据的扬州路 177 号酒行进行监视。

1939年1月13日下午4点，一辆由一名中国男性驾驶、载有3名乘客（2名日本人和1名中国人）的机动车 1542 号抵达并停在投诉人店铺门前。该中国人立即质问店主为何未向“税务局”汇款，当店主表示无钱时，该中国人陪同2名日本人进入店内，告知店主前往仓库，该仓库是一间中式房屋，位于店铺后门穿过巷弄对面，地址为韬朋路 122 弄 3 号，他们将因店主未付款而封存12坛酒。这12坛酒价值 250.00 美元。

执勤的4名侦探之一的华籍侦探 C.D.C. 220 立即与警署联系，具名人随同侦探长史密斯（Smith）、高级督察戴维斯（Davies）和华籍探员 J.P.C. 71 赶赴现场。

到达店铺后，司机被扣留；进入韬朋路 122 弄 3 号后，观察到2名日本人和1名中国人正在用封条封存投诉人的酒坛，封条翻译如下：-

“江兴酒行。由江苏省卷烟酒类税务局封存。日期 1939年1月12日，盖有江苏省卷烟酒类税务局印章”
（原报告附有一枚封条）。

当被告知具名人为工部局警务处代表，且他们无权封存投诉人财产或对其征税和罚款时，他们回答称来自税务局，奉命封存投诉人财产。这3人

（左侧边缘印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 还押监 / 1939年1月16日）

Subject Illegal Functioning of Japanese and Chinese employed by
the Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei Tax Bureau.
Made by D. I. Hutton Forwarded by

Sir:
At 2.15 p.m. 12/1/39 a male Chinese named Woo Ying Daung
( 吴应堂 ) 42, native of Kiangying, wine shop proprietor, residing
at and operating a wine shop at 177 Yangchow Road reported that
at 10.30 a.m. 12/1/39 one Japanese accompanied by 4 Chinese
arrived at his shop in a motor car Lic. Numbers unknown.
One of the Chinese known to complainant by the name of
"Zang" ( 张 ) questioned complt. as to the reason he had failed
to register his wine shop with the Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei
Wine Tax Bureau. Complt. stated he would visit the office at
4 p.m. 12/1/39. "Zang" then took one account book and 2 invoices
for wine supplied by "Kiangying Woo Yyi" wine shop and informed
complt. that should he fail to register and pay the tax of
$45.00 per month his shop would be closed and he would be stopped
from doing further business, and in addition to the tax he would
require to pay $75.00 fine as he had operated the wine shop for
a considerable time without have registered or paid his taxes.
Complt. agreed to visit the Tax Office and was further informed
that should he fail to attend he would be arrested and handed
over to the Japanese Military Police. One of the 4 Chinese named
"Yih" ( 叶 ) then informed the Japanese that complt. had failed
to carry out instructions and the Japanese struck complt. on the
face with his open hand.
The names of 3 of the Chinese was given as:-
Zang ( 张 ),
Sung ( 陈 ),
Yih ( 叶 )
One unknown.

先生：
1939年1月12日下午2时15分，一名名叫吴应堂 (Woo Ying Daung) 的华籍男子，42岁，江苏江阴人，酒店店主，居住并经营扬州路177号的酒店，前来报案称：1939年1月12日上午10时30分，一名日本人 accompanied by 四名华人乘坐一辆汽车（车牌号码不详）到达他的店铺。
其中一名报案人认识的华人，名叫“张” (Zang)，质问报案人为何未向江苏、浙江及安徽酒税局登记其酒店。报案人称他将于1939年1月12日下午4时前往该局办公室。“张”随后拿走一本账簿和两张由“江阴吴义”酒店供应酒的发票，并告知报案人，如果他不去登记并缴纳每月45.00元的税款，他的店铺将被查封，并被禁止继续营业；此外，由于他在相当长的一段时间内未登记或纳税而经营酒店，除税款外，还需缴纳75.00元罚款。报案人同意前往税务局，并进一步被告知，如果他不去，将被逮捕并移交给日本宪兵队。四名华人中一名名叫“叶” (Yih) 的人随后告诉日本人，报案人未执行指令，日本人便用手掌打了报案人的脸。
其中三名华人的姓名如下：
张 (Zang)，
陈 (Sung)，
叶 (Yih)
一人不知名。

Subject Alleged Illegal Functioning of Outside Authorities.

Made by D.S.I. Willrose Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir:
At 5.20 p.m. 11/1/39 one Zu Yue Kung (華有根) shop assistant of the Yih Tai Tobacco Shop 376 Ward Road came to the station and reported that at about 4 p.m. 10/1/39, 2 Japanese and a Chinese in plain clothes arrived at his shop in a M/car License Number unknown. They were equiped with round blue coloured badges. After an inspection of the stock the undermentioned cigarettes were selected and taken together with the assistant to house 13 Yih Woo Lee off Chapoo Road.
(1) 36 packets of "Three coppers" cigarettes,
(2) 2 packets "Holeise" cigarettes,
(3) 1 packet "Flying Dragon" cigarettes.
After lengthy questioning regarding the origin of the cigarettes, the shop assistant was released with instructions to return at 9 a.m. 11/1/39. At the stated time the assistant attended at house 13, Yih Woo Lee off Chapoo Road when he was informed that with the exception of the 2 packets of "Holeisi" cigarettes which were returned to him, the seized cigarettes were to be confiscated because they had not been registered with the Reformed Government of China.
The Japanese Consular Police were requested by Yulin Road Station for any information in their possession regarding a tax office at No. 13 Yih Woo Lee Chapoo Road and after making enquiries they informed the station that it was a branch of the General Revenue Office of Kiangsu, Chekiang & Anhwei Provinces.

[Signature]
Sen. Det. Lt.
D.D.O. (D) Division.

[Signature]
13/1

[Signature]
D.S.I.

先生：
1939年1月11日下午5时20分，华德路376号益泰烟草店店员朱有根 (Zu Yue Kung)（原文此处中文名写作華有根，结合上下文及p122应为朱有根，但依要求保留原文拼写对应的音译或注明，此处原文为 Zu Yue Kung (華有根)，照实翻译为朱有根 (Zu Yue Kung) 并在括号内保留原文汉字差异或按前文统一，考虑到前文已确认为朱有根，此处括号内原文为“華有根”，可能是笔误，依要求“照实译出”，故译为：朱有根 (Zu Yue Kung) [原文注：華有根]）来到警署报案称：1939年1月10日下午4时许，两名日本人和一名便衣华人乘坐一辆汽车（车牌号码不详）到达他的店铺。他们佩戴着圆形的蓝色徽章。在检查库存后，选出了下列香烟，并将店员带往乍浦路亿伍里13号住宅。
(1) 36包“三铜板”香烟，
(2) 2包“好利司” (Holeise) 香烟，
(3) 1包“飞龙”香烟。
经过长时间关于香烟来源的讯问后，店员被释放，并被告知于1939年1月11日上午9时返回。在规定时间，店员前往乍浦路亿伍里13号，被告知除了退还给他的2包“好利司”香烟外，其余被扣香烟将被没收，理由是这些香烟未向中华民国维新政府登记。

榆林路捕房向日本领事馆警察查询其掌握的关于乍浦路亿伍里13号税务办公室的任何信息，经查询后，他们告知捕房，那是江苏、浙江及安徽三省统税局的分局。

1938年11月10日上午11时45分，中央捕房警员3320将两名自称为以下身份的华籍男子带到警署：

1. 高祈武 (Kau Sing Woo)，36岁，安徽人，住福州路295号。

警员3320报告称，1938年11月10日上午10时30分至10时45分之间，警察看到上述人员拦截了三辆卡车，车牌号分别为23566、23501和23192，当时这些车辆正装载煤炭离开外滩3号浮码头。根据比爾 (Beer) 副督察的指令，这两人被逮捕并带至中央捕房。

J.I.O. 21. 10. 38. (李耀三)
B'well Stn. 21/10/38.

On the 21/10/38, I was
at my duty at the corner of Connaught & Jessfield
Road. At about 4.15 p.m. a crowd of people came down from a
terrace at 562 Jessfield Road, corner of Connaught
Road, and walked South along Jessfield Road. At the same time,
four Trooper S.P.C.s were patrolling from South to North and
seeing this crowd running in different directions, two of them
dismounted and gave chase and arrested one of them. At this
time, I heard someone shouting that one of the men was armed
with a pistol. I gave chase South along Jessfield Road and
when about thirty yards from my duty post, I saw two men
fighting outside a canned-goods shop. I arrested both and
saw that one of them was armed with a pistol. I took down this
pistol, asked them the reason for fighting and the armed man's
occupation, but this man refused to answer. With the assistance
of the S.P.C. I took both parties to the B'well Station. Whilst
on our way to the station near the Ta Tao Police Bureau, the
armed man told me that he was a detective attached to the Ta
Tao Police. I asked him to show his warrant card. He told
me that he had forgotten to bring it along with him and wanted
to get it from the Ta Tao Police Bureau. Fearing that
something may happen, I refused and only gave him permission
to inform the Police on Ta Tao Police Bureau gate. When reaching
the Ta Tao Police Bureau, he refused to follow me and at the same
time a number of Ta Tao Police, detectives and Japanese Military
Police, came out of the Bureau and forcibly took me to their
office, took away my pistol and did not allow me to say anything.

The above is my true statement.

(Sgd.) Lee Yao San

静安寺捕房 1938年10月21日。

1938年10月21日，我
在康纳脱路与极司菲尔路转角处执勤。下午4时15分左右，一群人从康纳脱路拐角处的极司菲尔路562号露台下来，沿极司菲尔路向南行走。与此同时，四名骑警巡官正由南向北巡逻，看到这群人向不同方向奔跑，其中两人下马追赶并逮捕了其中一人。此时，我听到有人喊叫，称其中一人持有手枪。我沿极司菲尔路向南追赶，在距离我的执勤岗位约三十码处，我看到两人在一家罐头食品店外打斗。我将两人逮捕，并发现其中一人持有手枪。我缴下了这把手枪，询问他们打斗的原因以及持枪者的职业，但此人拒绝回答。在骑警巡官的协助下，我将双方带往静安寺捕房。在前往捕房途中，靠近大道警察局时，持枪者告诉我他是大道警察所属的侦探。我要求他出示委任证。他告诉我忘记随身携带，想从大道警察局取来。由于担心发生意外，我拒绝了，只允许他在大道警察局门口通知警方。到达大道警察局时，他拒绝跟随我，同时多名大道警察、侦探和日本宪兵从局内出来，强行将我带到他们的办公室，拿走了我的手枪，并不让我说任何话。

以上是我的真实陈述。

（签名）李耀三

Sir,

At 3.50 p.m. on the 24.10.38., a telephone message was received from the Foh Shing Tobacco Factory, No. 521 Macao Road to the effect that some Japanese had entered the factory and were going to arrest some of the workers.

D.S.I. Chao Ping Kun, J.D.S. 48 Mori and the undersigned attended when the following was ascertained:-

At about 3.30 p.m. 24.10.38., a Mr. Kanza Muratani, Tax Inspector attached to the Head Office of the Kiangsu Chekiang and Anhwei Provinces Tax Bureau No. 230 KiuKian Road accompanied by one Kokumu Kawashima a Chinese interpreter named Tsu Kyung Voong ( ) a clerk named Wong Sau Foo ( ) and one Tsang Tsze Fah ( ), the last 3 named being attached to the Bureau whilst the latter is an informer to Muratani, entered the factory as a result of information received by the Bureau Head Office during the last two months that the Foh Shing Factory Proprietors were evading the Tobacco Tax in as much as that they would send out cases of 50,000 cigarettes taxed $100.0 per case, then the same cases would be brought back to the factory repacked and the old stamps used again, his object being to inspect the factory and examine the books re the amount of cigarettes manufactured on the premises, and number of cases sent out. When he and his party entered the premises the only person in the offices was Wong Chung Kong ( ) Personal Manager and he did not feel inclined to allow them this privilege due to the fact that the manufacture and sales of the cigarettes were not under his supervision and further that he thought permission should be first obtained from Mr. Urey of the Union Tobacco Corporation, No. 51 Canton Road (Who during the absence on leave of Mr. Vines a partner in the firm)

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Road Coolies employed by the Shanghai Ta Tao City Government function in the Settlement.

Sir,

During the afternoon of October 10, 1938, eight coolies employed by the Shanghai Ta Tao City Government were observed to be levelling and spreading ashes on that part of MUKDEN ROAD located between East Kashing Road and Urqa Road Bridge.

Inspector J. Watson and a party of police attended and instructed the coolies to stop work immediately.

The Chinese foreman explained that they had been instructed to do the work by a Japanese Marine, who was in charge of them.

Sergeant KAKUYA of the Japanese Naval Landing Party subsequently attended Kashing Road Station and stated that the coolies had been loaned to them for the purpose of repairing the road in question.

It appears that Naval transports frequently use the road and that the authorities consider its present condition unsatisfactory.

It was explained to Sergeant Kakeya that the road was within the Settlement boundary and that the work should be done by the P.W.D.

The road is nothing more than a cinder path and vehicles using it do so at their own risk.

受上海大道市政府雇用的道路苦力在租界内活动。

先生，

1938年10月10日下午，观察到八名受上海大道市政府雇用的苦力在位于东嘉兴路和乌尔嘎路桥之间的慕敦路路段平整和铺设煤灰。

沃森（J. Watson）督察及一队警察到场，指令苦力立即停止工作。

中国工头解释说，他们是受一名负责指挥他们的日本海军陆战队员的指示进行此项工作的。

随后，日本海军陆战队的加久屋（KAKUYA）军曹来到嘉兴路捕房，称这些苦力是借给他们用于修复该道路的。

看来海军运输车辆经常使用该道路，当局认为其目前状况令人不满。

已向加久屋军曹解释，该道路位于租界边界内，相关工作应由工务处进行。

该道路不过是一条煤渣路，车辆使用需自负风险。

Alleged Ta Tao Officials Operating on Singapore

At 4.30 p.m. on the 23/9/38, a female named Tsah
Sung Sz (蔡孫氏) the owner of the Western Dairy 45 Singa-
pore Road O.C.L. came to the station and reported that at
11 a.m. even date, three Chinese and 2 Japanese dressed
in foreign clothing came to her dairy and demanded that
she move out.

Enquiries by D.S.Daly and C.D. S.299 elicited that
the original owner of the dairy the father-in-law of the
informant, had died a few years ago, leaving the dairy to
his daughter-in-law with a stipulation that she pay a cer-
tain sum to his son,(her husband) whom the old man had
disowned on account of his bad habits.

The informant states that she has already paid
over the stipulated sum to her husband (who does not live
with her) and has certificates to prove her ownership of
the dairy.

The five men who called at 11 a.m. even date sta-
ted that they were employees of the Ta Tao Government who
were representing her husband and as the latter person
claimed and the dairy as his property, they ordered her
to move out and a few minutes later left the premises.

据称大道政府官员在新加坡路活动

1938年9月23日下午4时30分，一名名为 Tsah Sung Sz (蔡孫氏) 的女子来到警署报案。她是新加坡路45号（越界筑路区）西方乳品店 (Western Dairy) 的店主。她报告称，当日上午11时，三名华人和两名身着西式服装的日本人来到她的乳品店，要求她搬离。

经 Daly 副督察和警员 S.299 查询得知，该乳品店原业主为报案人的公公，已于数年前去世，将乳品店留给儿媳，但规定她需向其子（即其丈夫）支付一定金额。老人因其子恶习累累而与其断绝关系。

报案人称，她已向丈夫（未与她同住）支付了规定金额，并持有证明其拥有该乳品店所有权的证书。

当日中午11时到访的五名男子声称，他们是大道政府的雇员，代表其丈夫行事；鉴于后者声称该乳品店为其财产，他们命令她搬离，几分钟后离开了现场。

由于这极有可能是报案人丈夫企图向其妻子勒索钱财，已警告后者，若这些人或其他人再次光顾其乳品店，应立即通知 **〔此处转录不清〕**

先生，

1938年9月6日下午3时25分，警员 C.D.C. 85号将三名男性华人带至警署，分别是：Zee Yoong Zai (徐永才)，32岁，常州人，职业/船主；Tsoo Yoong Yoong (祝永榮)，33岁，无锡人，职业/大道船舶登记局督察，居住于罗宾森路 (Robison Road) 75号（越界筑路区）；Tsai Yoong Sung (蔡永松)，29岁，苏州人，职业/无业，居住于布伦安路 (Brenan Road)（越界筑路区）。他因争吵在西苏州路近宜昌路处逮捕了他们，第一名指控第二和第三名向他勒索钱财。

经警员 C.D.C. 229号和本人查询，查明如下情况。

1938年9月6日下午，Tsoo Yoong Yoong 根据位于 Chapel 吴淞路的大道船舶登记局的指示，从西苏州路登上停泊在苏州河南岸的船只。作为督察，他核实这些船只是否已在该局注册，若未注册，则向其发放申请表，并指示船主填写表格后送至该局办公室进行注册，从而获得在日本控制区航行所需的必要通行证。

1938年9月6日下午3时许，他登上了 Zee Yoong Zai 拥有的4601号船，发现该船已注册货运但未注册客运，因此告知 Zee，他将因同时使用船只进行客运和货运而向局里报告，并告诉 Zee 必须前往局办公室办理客运通行证。

Zee 不愿照办，请求 Tsoo 不要

1.

Complaint of the U.B.Brewery regarding
the Illegal functioning of the Consolidated
Tax Bureau of the Newly Reformed Government.

At 3.50.p.m. on 30.8.1938 Chief Insp. Barry
in charge Central Station, received a telephone message
from D.S.Pitts, Special Branch, to the effect that the
Consolidated Tax Bureau officials had detained cargo of
the U.B.Brewery (240 cases of beer) at Foochow Road
Jetty. Chief Insp. Barry, D.S.I.Guess, D.S.Pitts,
S.I.Zee and B.S.I.Kau (Sp.Br), proceeded at once to the
jetty and found everything quiet but three males, apparently
Japanese, aboard the lighter loaded with beer.

S.I.Oikawa and J.D.C.Yoshinaga were then called
to the scene but on their arrival the Japanese had al-
ready left the boat. A Chinese who was recognised as a
member of the trio was found on the jetty and when quest-
ioned by J.D.S.Yoshinaga this man gave his name as Woo
Liang (吴良) and the names of the Japanese as M.Maeda
(前田松夫) and Satoh (佐藤) all of whom were connected
with the Consolidated Tax Bureau, 230 Kiukiang Road.

From enquiries made by D.S.I.Guess it appears
that at about 2.00.p.m. on 30.8.1938 210 cases of beer
were passed through the Customs and tax paid. The cargo
was then loaded onto a lighter at No.6 Pontoon in readi-
ness for removal to the S.S. Peking for transshipment
to Singapore.

interpreter. Actually no direct action was taken to
detain or remove the cargo. Owing to the fact that the
owners apparently refused to move the cargo into the
river the Tax Bureau Representatives left after the
arrival of the S.M.Police.

Mr.O'Neill of the Union Brewery was questioned
by D.I.Guoss and admitted that no effort was made to
interfere with the cargo or to remove the lighter but it
was quite obvious that once in midstream the lighter and
contents would have been seized and it was therefore de-
cided to return the cargo to the godown until some arrang-
ements have been made between the Tax Bureau and the
British Embassy who are handling the affair.

It appears that the Union Brewery are willing to
pay the Tax Bureau but at the same time refuse to acknow-
ledge the Reformed Government Tax Bureau. They have on
previous occasions paid the tax through a third party but
the Tax Bureau has now refused to accept payment in this
manner, apparently in an attempt to force recognition.

The foregoing details were made known to Mr.A.H.
Aoirs, D.O."A" Division and with his consent Woo Liang
was released after advice that lighters etc tied to
the Pontoons were considered within the Jurisdiction of
the S.M.P. and beyond the control of the Tax Bureau and
that functioning on such craft might result in arrest.

翻译。实际上并未采取直接行动扣押或移走货物。由于货主显然拒绝将货物移入河中，在工部局警务处人员到达后，税务局代表离去。

联合啤酒厂的 O'Neill 先生接受 Guoss 侦探督察的讯问，并承认未努力干涉货物或移走驳船，但很明显，一旦驳船进入河中心，驳船及其内容物将被扣押，因此决定将货物退回仓库，直到税务局与正在处理此事的英国大使馆之间做出某些安排。

看来联合啤酒厂愿意向税务局缴纳税款，但同时拒绝承认维新政府税务局。他们此前曾通过第三方缴纳税款，但税务局现在拒绝以这种方式接受付款，显然是为了迫使对方承认其地位。

上述详情已告知“A”区警务总监 Aoirs 先生 (Mr.A.H. Aoirs)，并经其同意，在告知系于浮筒的驳船等被视为在工部局警务处管辖范围内，超出税务局控制权，且在此类船只上活动可能导致逮捕后，Woo Liang 获释。

The Acting Secretary.

The position of the Kiangse, Chekiang, and Anhwei
Revenue Bureau solely with regard to the Rolled Tobacco Tax
was discussed informally with the Senior Consul and the
American, British and French Consuls-General some months ago
and it was thought that in view of the agreement between the
Consular Body and the Nationalist Government of China and in
view of the importance of the matter to foreign tobacco mer-
chants that while no official recognition should be given to
this Bureau under the existing regime, it might be in the
interest of the tobacco merchants to tacitly acquiesce in the
new regime carrying on upon the basis of the old agreement.

There never has been any agreement between the
Consular Body or the Council and the Nationalist Government
about the collection in the Settlement of taxes upon any
other articles than rolled tobacco.

As this bureau does not confine itself to the for-
mer agreement and is interfering with various lines of bus-
iness I think the Police should take every practical step
to prevent the officials of this bureau from functioning
either in the Settlement or on the extra-Settlement roads.

In so far as I am aware the breweries in the past
have made their own private arrangements with the Tax Bureau
and have not called upon the Council for any assistance.

According to reports the officials of the present
bureau are more or less corrupt but I do not feel the
bureau should be given any consideration whatever on the part
of the Council.

(sd) Stirling Fessenden
Secretary General.

代理秘书。

数月前，曾就江西、浙江及安徽税务局仅涉及卷烟税的立场问题，与首席领事以及美国、英国和法国总领事进行了非正式讨论。鉴于领事团与中国国民政府之间的协议，以及此事对外国烟草商的重要性，大家认为，虽然在现有体制下不应给予该局任何官方承认，但为了烟草商的利益，不妨默许新政权在旧协议的基础上继续运作。

领事团或工部局与中国国民政府之间，从未就除卷烟以外的任何其他商品在租界内的征税问题达成过任何协议。

由于该局并不局限于先前的协议范围，且干涉了各种商业活动，我认为警方应采取一切实际措施，防止该局官员在租界内或越界筑路区域行使职权。

据我所知，过去的啤酒厂已与税务局自行达成私人安排，并未请求工部局提供任何协助。

据报告，现任该局的官员或多或少存在腐败行为，但我认为工部局不应给予该局任何考虑。

（签名）斯特林·费森登

Further to the attached Bubbling Well Station
Miscellaneous Report No.295/38 regarding the seizure from one
Wong Zai Pao of 144 bottles of mineral waters on Jessfield
Road, on July 19tn, by a police constable attached to the
Singapore Police Sub-Station of the Pootung Police Bureau,

inspectors are sent out daily to the Western outside road

stamps.

1.

Illegal Functioning of "Ta Tao" Government Official
on Jessfield Road, C.R.D.

At 11a.m. 19/7/38, Vong Sai Pao (王財宝), coolie,
employed Mr. Iung Ts Ling ( 殷子林 ), undertaker, 55
Kiamoor Road, was sent to this station by his master
with the following complaint:-

At 9a.m. 19/7/38 the coolie was instructed by Mr.
Iung Ts Ling to carry 144 bottles of various kinds of
mineral waters from his office, 827 Haiphong Road to his
residence, 55 Kiamoor Road.

He loaded the mineral waters on to a hand-trolly,
and set out on his errand.

At 9.30a.m. 19/7/38, at Jessfield Road near
Connaught Road, the coolie was stopped by a male Chinese
dressed in a long black gown, and speaking Shanghai
dialect, who produced a "Ta Tao" Government warrant card
bearing his photograph, and then examined the mineral
water. The "Ta Tao" Government official notified the
coolie that the bottles did not bear any "Ta Tao" revenue

1938年7月19日上午11时，苦力Vong Sai Pao（王財宝），受雇于胶州路55号殡仪馆老板殷子林先生，由其主人派至本捕房提出以下投诉：-

1938年7月19日上午9时，殷子林先生指示该苦力将其位于海防路827号的办事处内的144瓶各类矿泉水运送至其位于胶州路55号的住所。

他将矿泉水装上手推车，开始执行任务。

1938年7月19日上午9时30分，在极司菲尔路靠近康纳路处，该苦力被一名身穿黑色长袍、讲上海话的中国男子拦下，该男子出示了一张印有其照片的“大陶”政府委任证，随后检查了矿泉水。该“大陶”政府官员通知苦力，这些瓶子未贴有任何“大陶”税务印花，因此必须扣留该财产。

该苦力被带往极司菲尔路473号（门牌号）的一处“大陶”政府办公室，那里的144瓶矿泉水被从他手中拿走，记录了他的姓名和地址，并被告知将处以罚款。关于外貌和陈述的细节

涉嫌九江路230号统税局非法行使职权。

1938年6月12日上午11时15分，中国侦探警员940号向捕房报告，发现一名叫李虎誠的人，系九江路230号统税局所属的第6号侦探警员，当时他持有5包包含各品牌香烟的纸箱。被捕者称，他正将这些物品送往九江路的统税局总部，因未缴纳税款而予以没收。

“Ta-Tao Government”
Tax Collector Faces
Extortion Charges

Facing a charge of extortion,
a man, who claimed to be a tax-
collector of the “Ta Tao” ad-
ministration, yesterday morning
appeared in the First Special
District Court on a writ of
detention application of the
Settlement police.

The accused, who gave his
name as Wang Scu-tsang, was
arrested Sunday afternoon when
he attempted to collect a “tax”
of $1.20 on each head of pigs
from farmers.

Wang, according to the state-
ment made by the municipal ad-
vocate, had established himself
as a “tax collector” at No. 12
pontoon and was in the process
of enforcing the levy when he
was taken into custody by a
Chinese police constable.

The writ of detention was
granted by the Court and the
case was remanded for one week.

〔此处转录不清〕

“大陶政府”
税务员面临
勒索指控

一名自称是“大陶”行政当局税务员的男子，因面临勒索指控，昨天上午根据租界警方的拘留申请令，在第一特区法院出庭。

被告自称为Wang Scu-tsang，周日下午当他试图向农民收取每头猪1.20美元的“税款”时被捕。

据市政检察官陈述，Wang在12号浮码头设立了“税务员”身份，并在强行征收税款时被一名中国警员拘捕。

法院批准了拘留令，案件延期一周审理。

00801

TAX COLLECTOR IS
TAKEN TO COURT

Settlement Police Are
Looking For Illegal
Agents Along Bund

The intention of the Settlement
authorities to frustrate any attempt
made by tax collectors of the
"Great Way" City Government to
collect tax money in areas under
their jurisdiction was indicated
yesterday in the First Special Dis-
trict Court when Wang Sau-tsang,
one of several "Great Way" regime
tax collectors operating along The
Bund was brought up on a writ of
detention. Hearing was postponed
for a week pending further in-
vestigations.
Wang was arrested last Saturday
near the Nanking Road Bund
where he and several of his col-
leagues, all armed with badges,
were seen arguing with some boat-
men whose boat was moored along-
side the jetty. They were trying to
collect what they termed the "cargo
tax" on pigs and chickens which
the boatmen were trying to unload.
Wang was caught at the height of
the dispute, but the colleagues man-
aged to escape during the con-
fusion.

（批：file d 24/5）
（批：B 24/5）
pages.zh:
00801

税务员被
带上法庭

租界警方正在
外滩搜寻非法
代理人

租界当局挫败“大道”市政府税务员在其管辖区域内收税的任何企图，这一意图昨天在第一特区法院得到体现，当时几名在外滩活动的“大道”政权税务员之一的Wang Sau-tsang因拘留令被带上法庭。听证会推迟一周，以待进一步调查。
Wang上周六在南京路外滩附近被捕，当时有人看到他和几名同事，都佩戴徽章，正与一些停靠在码头旁船只的船夫争论。他们试图对船夫们正试图卸下的猪和鸡收取所谓的“货物税”。Wang在争执最激烈时被抓，但他的同事们在混乱中设法逃脱。

（批：归档 5月24日）
（批：B 5月24日）

correct name as Wong Lih Dong (王立東) Chief Inspector of
the "Shanghai Municipality Ministry of Finance Cattle and
Poultry Tax Bureau". He identified the accused as being
employed by the Bureau and stated that he had instructed
him to go to The Bund in order to inform all cattle and
poultry dealers that they must register with the Bureau
before the 20th of this month. He further stated that

He has made a statement to this effect which is attached
herewith.

A statement was then taken from the accused in which

He denies having demanded any money, stating that
another inspector named Yang was the man who demanded the
$1.20 per head tax. He further states that he was original
employed as a teaboy at the Bureau.

C.P.C. 993 attached to Central Stn.
xx
Central Stn.          21-5-38

C.P.C. 993 reports as follows:-
Between 4p.m. and 10p.m. or the 20th inst. I was on duty at
No. 12 Foochow, The Bund. At about 6.30p.m. same date I was
approached by a well dressed male Chinese who represented himself
as a Tax Collector attached to the "Tah Dao" Government and
requested me to bring the pig dealers to the station, because the
latter had violated the Tax Regulations and refused to pay the
required tax i.e. $1.20 for each pig. I asked the above Chinese
whether he could produce any proof to verify that he was a bona
fide officer, upon which he showed me a badge bearing his name.
I then replied to this man that no tax whatsoever could be
collected within the precincts of the International Settlement.
In the meantime a foreign Inspector happened to come to the scene
and after having reported the matter to the Inspector, he
instructed me to bring the alleged tax inspector to the station.
                                        Signed.

华籍巡捕993号报告如下：

本月20日下午4时至10时期间，我在外滩福州路12号执勤。同日约下午6时30分，一名衣着体面的中国男子上前与我接触，自称是“大道”政府所属的税务征收员，并要求我将猪贩带往捕房，理由是后者违反税务条例，拒绝缴纳规定税款，即每头猪1.20元。我问上述中国人能否出示任何证明以证实其为正式官员，随即他向我展示了一枚印有他姓名的徽章。我于是回答此人，在国际租界范围内不得征收任何税款。此时，一名外籍督察恰好来到现场，在向该督察报告此事后，他指示我将这名所谓的税务稽查员带往捕房。
                                        签名。

States:-

At 8.30 a.m. on the 20/5/38, I was employed as a teeboy by
the Poultry Tax Bureau situated at Room 705, 33 Szechuen Road.
At 2 p.m. same date, I was instructed by Wong Li Dong (王立
堂) to accompany two other persons namely Yang (杨) and
Soong (宋) to proceed to the various pontoons on the Bund
and make enquiries among the poultry dealers, who ship their
cargoes from Kompo, regarding "Purchasing Permits", and to
advise them to obtain same from the above tax bureau should
they fail to produce any, as the bureau was established only
recently and they were unaware of this procedure.

At 6 p.m. same date, on approaching the No. 14 Pontoon, we
observed a boat lying alongside loaded with more than one hundred
pigs. Yang then went onto the pontoon and talked to the men in
the boat. I and Soong did not hear their conversation. About
10 minutes later, we also boarded the pontoon. Yang then advised
me to report the matter to Wong Li Dong by telephone. I did so.
A few minutes later, Wong Li Dong came and consulted with Yang.
We did not know what they talked. After this, Yang again asked
the men on the boat if their master were on the boat and whether
or not they had obtained a "Purchasing Permit". The men in the
boat replied in the negative. Yang then told them that as they
could not produce a "Purchasing Permit" they would have to pay a
tax of $1.20 for each head of pig. This they refused. Then we
all came to the Bund and Yang informed Wong Li Dong of the result
Whereupon the latter instructed me to call a C.P.C. and request
him to arrest 2 or 3 of the men. I then approached C.P.C. 988

陈述如下：

1938年5月20日上午8时30分，我被受雇为四川路33号705室家禽税局的茶役。同日下午2时，我奉王立堂（Wong Li Dong）之命，陪同另外两人，即杨某（Yang）和宋某（Soong），前往外滩各浮码头，向从高邮（Kompo，音译）运货的家禽商人查询“购买许可证”事宜，并告知他们若无法出示许可证，应向上述税局申领，因为该局刚成立不久，他们尚不了解此程序。

同日下午6时，当我们接近14号码头时，发现一艘船停靠在旁，装载着一百多头猪。杨某随后走上码头与船上人员交谈。我和宋某未听到他们的谈话内容。约10分钟后，我们也登上了码头。杨某随后让我通过电话向王立堂汇报此事。我照办了。几分钟后，王立堂到来并与杨某商议。我们不知他们谈了什么。此后，杨某再次询问船上人员其主人是否在船上，以及是否已获取“购买许可证”。船上人员予以否认。杨某随后告诉他们，由于无法出示“购买许可证”，他们必须按每头猪1.20元缴纳税款。对方拒绝支付。于是我们全部回到外滩，杨某将结果告知王立堂。后者随即指示我叫来一名华籍巡捕，并请其逮捕其中两三人。我随后走近华籍巡捕988号

1938年5月20日晚7时，华籍巡捕993号从外滩12号码头将一名名叫黄寿章（Wong Seu Tsang）的男子带至捕房。黄，26岁，上海人，前税务稽查员，住法租界陶尔斐司路吉安里274号。巡捕观察到其试图在外滩向猪贩收税。

经刑事侦缉处287号警探及本人调查，查明情况如下：

（批注：特高科副本）

1938年5月20日晚6时45分左右，华籍巡捕993号观察到黄姓男子与几名正在外滩卸猪的人员发生争执，这些人员持有海关和公共卫生处（P.H.D.）的许可证。上前询问后得知，此人自称是改组后的上海市政府税务局官员，要求对所有卸在外滩的猪按每头1.20元征税。各位猪贩拒绝支付，因此华籍巡捕将黄姓男子带至捕房。他在捕房出示了一枚丝绸徽章，上面用汉字写着：“督办上海市政公署财政局牲畜税稽征所稽查员第四号黄寿章”。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 1938年5月21日 / 特高科）

    At 10.45p.m. two named Lieu Yee Dien (刘福田) and

    The circumstances of the case were explained

今天早晨才开设，并由一位王先生发给徽章，指示他在下午5时接管12号码头，并对在该码头卸下的所有猪按每头1.20元收税。他还称，他的指示是，如果有人拒绝付款，就叫警察。他将留在那里，直到王先生来换班。
    警探走访了四川路33号的办公室，发现那是七楼一间新开设的小办公室。当时只有一名苦力在内，他表示不知道主人的地址，并称主人要到第二天早上才会来。

    晚上10时45分，两名名叫刘福田（Lieu Yee Dien）和郑应奎（Tsung Ing Kwei）的男子来到捕房，请求释放被告，被告系前者的亲属。后者是日本军方特务机关（Special Service Section）雇佣的翻译，办公地点在毕勋路719号。他们提供了被拘留者提到的“王”姓男子的姓名为王立生（Wang Lee Sing），但不知道其地址。

Enquiries made by C.D... 16C and the undersigned
ascertained the following:- C.P.C. 2161 on post duty
at Nanking Rd. and The Bund at about 11p.m. 22/5/38
observed a large number of persons assembled together
outside the bamboo fence erected on the east side of
the new Bund Rd., he therefore attended to ascertain
the cause of same when the persons involved attempted
to disperse, but he was able to effect the apprehension
of the principals as recorded above; From his subsequent
enquiries he learned that the boatman was in possession
of ten boxes of Ruby Queen cigarettes each containing
50 packets of ten cigarettes and was proceeding towards
his boat which was moored near to No. 13 Pontoon when he
was arrested and stopped by the two males described above.

1938年5月22日晚11时15分，华籍探员2161号陪同一名叫周阿四（Tsou Ah）的中国男子（28岁，宁波人，职业船夫，居住在货船上），从南京路和新外滩路将两名中国男子带至捕房，描述如下：

(1) 崔忠美（Shuin Taoong Yuin，音译），33岁，绍兴人，职业税务局雇员，九江路23C号。
(2) 周财宝（Chiu Tsei Pau），20岁，宁波人，职业无业，伯基尔路3号。

经刑事侦缉处16C号警探及本人调查，查明情况如下：1938年5月22日晚11点左右，华籍巡捕2161号在南京路和外滩执勤时，观察到大量人员聚集在新外滩路东侧搭建的竹篱笆外，于是他前去查明原因，当时涉案人员试图散开，但他成功抓获了上述主要嫌疑人；经后续调查，他得知船夫拥有十箱“红女王”（Ruby Queen）牌香烟，每箱装有50包，每包10支，正走向停靠在13号码头附近的船只时，被上述两名男子拦截并逮捕。

the second of whom used a small flash light in his
possession which he displayed on the cigarettes, the
other male produced a small badge which he exhibited
then declared that the tobacco tax for the cigarettes had not
been paid and requested that the complainant accompany
him to the office of his place of employment at
Nanking Rd. The complainant remonstrated which result-
ed in the usual crowd of curious onlookers gathering
round.

Upon the C.P.C.s arrival the first male produced
a small badge which only indicated his place of
employment bearing characters: "Kiangsu, Chekiang and

统税局)" which
subsequently resulted in his being brought to the station
together with the other males concerned.

From the above it appears that the two males concern-
ed had attempted to extort money from the complainant
for being in possession of cigarettes not bearing the
required stamp.

In view of the above and the lateness of the hour
at which the arrests were effected Mr. Aiers D.D.O."A".
Div. was communicated with who instructed that the two
males concerned be detained at this station until A.M.
23/5/38 pending explicit instructions being issued re.
pages.zh:
第2页。

其中第二名男子使用随身携带的小手电筒照射香烟，另一名男子则出示了一枚小徽章，随后宣称这些香烟未缴纳烟草税，并要求投诉人随他前往其位于南京路的任职机构办公室。投诉人提出抗议，结果引来了通常那样一群好奇的旁观者围观。

华籍巡捕到达后，第一名男子出示了一枚小徽章，上面仅标明其任职机构，字样为：“江苏浙江安徽统税局”，这导致他连同其他相关男子一起被带往捕房。

综上所述，这两名涉案男子似乎企图以投诉人持有未贴所需印花税票的香烟为由，向其勒索钱财。

鉴于上述情况及逮捕时间较晚，已与“A”区副总监艾尔斯先生（Mr. Aiers D.D.O."A". Div.）联系，他指示将这两名男子扣留在本捕房，直至1938年5月23日上午，等待有关

he knew nothing about the case except that a Japanese
Inspector named Mayeda had sent the trucks in. This

Citizen Association from where the pass was obtained,
with the result that Mr. V.Z. Chow (周) of above body,

no right to stop or detain the trucks whatsoever and the

instructions that the trucks could be released and said
that Insp. Ling, Police Liaison Officer, would telephone
Mr. T. Thomas Cheyne later and inform him accordingly.

协会，结果是该机构的周先生（V.Z. Chow）来到巡捕房，带来了投诉人的通行证，他称该通行证已由日本海军陆战队、日本宪兵队和日本军队租界区指挥官通过，允许货物从占领区过境至法租界。
    综上所述，前田稽查员在未首先寻求工部局警务处协助的情况下扣留卡车，似乎属于非法行为，因此本人采访了布莱恩（R. J. Bryan Jun. M.A.）先生，他同意上述观点，并表示统税局无权以任何理由拦截或扣留卡车，所谓的“酒税”对于仅在租界或法租界内移动的货物不予承认。布莱恩先生指示可以释放卡车，并表示警察联络官凌督察（Insp. Ling）稍后将致电钱德之（T. Thomas Cheyne）先生并告知此事。
    因此，两辆卡车于下午4时被释放，并由警察护送至法租界边界。

关于1938年4月4日下午2时30分在海关码头扣押5箱啤酒（系爱多亚路七段67号福盛食品店财产）一事。

先生：

1938年4月4日下午4时40分，联合啤酒有限公司（Union Brewery, Ltd.）代表 P.T. O'Neill 先生，偕同爱多亚路七段67号福盛食品店经理顾成志（Kuh Zung Tse）来到巡捕房投诉，称其5箱价值90美元的联合啤酒厂啤酒于1938年4月4日下午2时30分在海关码头被新成立的统税局官员以未缴纳税款为由扣押，并被该局扣留。

后者进一步陈述，他曾前往该局，被罚款39.00美元（此金额显然包含13美元税款），同时被告知可以提走这5箱啤酒。然而，他将啤酒留在那间办公室，并立即联系了 O'Neill 先生（他最初是从 O'Neill 先生的公司购买这些啤酒的），O'Neill 先生随即向本巡捕房报案。

经查询得知，这几箱啤酒是从投诉人的商店（位于法租界）运至海关码头，目的是交付给停泊在吴淞的一艘电缆船。

经讯问，上述两人均承认本案中的酒税尚未缴纳，而 O'Neill 先生

REPORT

Subject Further to Misc. 20/38.

Made by J. I. Burton. Forwarded by Inspt. i/c.

Sir,

Further investigations in reference to the activities of the An Hui Tax Bureau, show that representatives of the Bureau are in attendance at the following mills.

Ting Yue No. 1 and 2 Mills, No. 37 West Soochow and No. 8 Moulson Roads respectively.

Tung Sing No. 2 and 3 Mills, No. 6, 16ang and 140 Macro Roads respectively.

Tung Yin Mill, No. 25 Lornan Road.

The mill managements of these concerns have no objection to these people being on the mill premises, they having reached an agreement whereby no money is paid in taxes on cotton yarn etc exported. The system they are now using is that all yarn etc taken out of the mills for exportation is tax assessed and recorded in account books by the Bureau representatives and receipts are issued, which enables goods to be passed by the Customs and loaded on ships.

It is understood that until all concerns British and Chinese, come to some agreement in reference to the Taxes levied by this Bureau, no money will be paid to them, although it is presumed that in the near future demands will be made by the Bureau for payments.

However, most of the yarn etc exported is to Canton and Hongkong and the Bureau state that they only wish to collect taxes on goods destined for ports in the areas which come under their control i.e. Anhwei, Chekiang and Kiangsu, nevertheless they are tax assessing all goods taken out of the mills and it would appear that they mean to collect the taxes on these goods, or they would not be recording and issuing receipts for same.

D. B. I.

报告

主题 继杂项档案 20/38。

由 J. I. Burton 制作。由负责督察转发。

先生：

关于安徽税务局活动的进一步调查显示，该局代表出席以下纱厂。

鼎丰第一和第二纱厂，分别位于西苏州路37号和慕尔鸣路8号。

通兴第二和第三纱厂，分别位于6号、16ang路和麦克罗路140号。

通益纱厂，位于劳纳路25号。

这些企业的厂方不反对这些人出现在厂区，因为他们已达成协议，对出口的棉纱等不支付税款。他们目前采用的制度是，所有从纱厂取出用于出口的棉纱等，均由该局代表进行税务评估并记入账簿，并开具收据，从而使货物能够通过海关并装船。

据悉，在所有英商和华商企业就该局征收的税款达成某种协议之前，不会向他们支付任何款项，尽管预计该局在不久的将来会提出付款要求。

然而，大部分出口的棉纱等是运往广州和香港的，该局声称他们只希望对运往其控制区域（即安徽、浙江和江苏）港口的货物征税，尽管如此，他们正在对所有从纱厂取出的货物进行税务评估，看来他们打算对这些货物征税，否则他们就不会记录并为此开具收据。

D. B. I.

Made by D. S. I. Burton. Forwarded by Officer i/c.

Sir,

In accordance with the remarks of D.C. Crime,
that the Dah Tou Tax Bureau employees should not function in the
Settlement until the approval of the Consular Body and Council
has been given, the undersigned, accompanied by D.S.I. Chao Ping
Kun, proceeded to the Tung Yih Cotton Mill, No. 25 Mokanshan Road,
this a.m. and warned the three Dah Tou Tax Bureau representatives
in attendance at the mill accordingly.

These men, who gave their names as Dau Vung Bai
( 陶文培 ), Kyung Ying Tsung ( 金椿 ) and Tsau Ts Ong
( 曹志鴻 ), stated that they had been posted at the mill on
orders from their Head Office, No. 230 Kiukiang Road, and would
return there for further instructions from one named Zau Suh Chun
( 邵式軍 ), who is the Officer in charge of the Bureau at
present.

Each man was in possession of a metal badge issued
by the Bureau, which is about one inch square with a blue enamel
centre on yellow back ground, on the enamel centre are the
characters, "General Tax Bureau of Kiangsu, Chekiang and Anhwei",
which is the only means of identification issued by the Bureau.

After warning these people it was learned from
the Mill Management that should they wish to export cotton yarn
they must pay these taxes and produce a receipt or the Customs
will not allow the yarn to be shipped, therefore cotton destined
for places outside the control of this Bureau in China will be
taxed again by the Chinese Authorities, thus the mill owners will
have to pay double taxes, and any yarn sold in the Settlement is
also taxed, making the burden of the mill owners heavy.

主题 继杂项报告 “P.R.” 26/38。

由 D. S. I. Burton 制作。由负责警官转发。

先生：

根据刑事组副总监的意见，即在领事团和公董局批准之前，大道税务局雇员不应在租界内行使职权，具名者在今日上午由赵平坤（Chao Ping Kun）副督察陪同，前往莫干山路25号通益棉纺厂，并据此警告在该厂的三名大道税务局代表。

这些人自报姓名为陶文培（Dau Vung Bai）、金椿（Kyung Ying Tsung）和曹志鸿（Tsau Ts Ong），声称他们是奉九江路230号总局的命令派驻该厂的，并将返回那里听取目前负责该局事务的邵式军（Zau Suh Chun）的进一步指示。

每人持有一枚由该局颁发的金属徽章，约为1英寸见方，黄色背景上有蓝色珐琅中心，珐琅中心刻有“苏浙皖统税局”字样，这是该局颁发的唯一身份证明。

警告这些人之后，从厂方管理层获悉，如果他们希望出口棉纱，就必须缴纳这些税款并出示收据，否则海关将不允许棉纱装运，因此运往中国境内该局控制范围以外地方的棉花将被中国当局再次征税，从而纱厂主不得不缴纳双重税款，而在租界内销售的任何棉纱也要征税，使得纱厂主的负担沉重。

（左侧印章及批注：上海公共租界警务处特务科 1938年2月16日；C.J.S.L. E 2月16日；8616/v 1000/42；DCSB. S.I. 2月16日。）

该局使用的收据与中国政府使用的收据相同，只是加盖了该局的额外印章。

看来海关认可该局开具的收据，如果警告各纱厂的该局代表不得行使职权，棉纱出口将会停止，因此具名者在收到进一步指示以及明确海关是否允许在没有该局收据的情况下出口棉纱之前， refrain from visiting other mills（暂不去其他纱厂）。

D.S.I.

“B”区副总监。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 26/38.
Road Station,
REPORT
Date 10.2.38. 19

Subject Representatives of the Dah Tou Tax Bureau visiting the Sing Yue No.2
Cotton Mill, attempting to collect taxes.

Made by D. S. I. Burton. Forwarded by Officer i/c.

Sir,

At 1:45 P.M. on 10.2.38., one named Ling Yih Tung
(林亦棟), Accountant employed at the Sing Yue No.2 Cotton
Mill, No.8 Robison Road, came to the station and reported that
at 10 a.m. even date, two male Chinese purporting to be
representatives of the Dah Tou Tax Bureau (大頭稅務收稅處) visited
the mill stating that they wished to collect taxes on cotton
goods manufactured at the mill on the same basis as that which
they previously paid to the National Government General Tax
Bureau (國民政府統稅局), but on being refused left the mill.

The undersigned visited the mill and from the
accountant learned that on the 5.2.38., two male Chinese, who
stated that they were tax collectors operating under the Dah
Tou City Government of Shanghai, one who gave his name as
Tsau Shien Mou (周顯模) and the other as Wong (  ),
visited the mill and stated that they wished to collect taxes
on goods manufactured at that mill and the Sing Yue No.1 Mill,
No.37 West Soochow Road, however, they were told that no
notification had been received By the mill management from the
Shanghai Cotton Association informing them that this tax should
be paid, or that members of the Dah Tou Tax Bureau should
function in the mill, and until such notification was received,
they could not allow them to stay on the mill premises, these
men then left the mill. On the 9.2.38., these two males again
called at the mill and were told the same again, and according-
ly left, returning at 10 a.m. this date, when being refused
again stated that they would return on the a.m. of 11.2.38.

"B" Division.
D. S. I.

（左侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / SPECIAL BRANCH / 11 FEB 1938）
（左侧手写批注：S.1 / DSR / 11/2 / C "2 / [此处字迹潦草]）

档案号：26/38。
路巡捕房，
报告
日期：1938年2月10日。19

事由：大头税务局代表访问新裕第二棉纺厂，试图征税。

呈报人：副督察伯顿（Burton）。转呈人：主管警官。

先生：

1938年2月10日下午1时45分，一名名为林亦棟（Ling Yih Tung）的男子来到本巡捕房报案。他是罗别根路8号新裕第二棉纺厂的会计。他称，当日上午10时，两名自称是大头税务局（大頭稅務收稅處）代表的中国男子到访该厂，声称希望按照此前向国民政府统税局（國民政府統稅局）缴纳税款的标准，对该厂生产的棉织品征税，但在遭到拒绝后离开了工厂。

本人随后走访了该厂，并从会计处获悉，1938年2月5日，两名中国男子到访该厂，声称他们是受上海大头市政府委派的税务征收员。其中一人自称周顯模（Tsau Shien Mou），另一人姓王（Wong）（  ）。他们表示希望对该厂以及西苏州路37号的新裕第一棉纺厂所生产的货物征税。然而，厂方告知他们，上海棉业同业公会尚未通知厂方需缴纳此项税款，也未通知大头税务局成员可在厂内行事；在收到此类通知之前，厂方不允许他们留在厂区。这些人随即离开。1938年2月9日，这两名男子再次到访，得到了同样的答复，于是离开。他们于今日上午10时返回，在再次被拒后声称将于1938年2月11日上午再来。

“B”区。
副督察。

（左侧印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 特务科 / 1938年2月11日）
（左侧手写批注：S.1 / DSR / 11/2 / C "2 / [此处字迹潦草]）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
West Hongkew Station,
REPORT
Date February 20, 1938.
Subject Illegal functioning by members of Consolidated Tax Bureau.
Made by ____ Cook Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At __ p.m. on February 20th 1938 Senior Police Constable
24 __ reported that he had arrested two Chinese, named:
(1) Lee Tuh (李__ ), age __ , native of Sungkiang, Consolida-
ted Tax Bureau Inspector No. 4, and
(2) Lee Kwen Jung (许坤__), age 48, native of Shanghai,
Consolidated Tax Bureau Inspector No. 9,
whom he arrested on both occasions near North Chekiang Road;
after being informed by one named Woo Sing Kung (伍星根), shop
assistant, employed by the Woo Chung Chu Pyi (华众__) Rice Shop,
house No. __ Alleyway, Tientsing Road, that they had
prevented him from loading two cases of cigarettes on a boat in
the Soochow Creek.

Subsequent enquiries made by V.C. 311 and the undersigned,
revealed that at about 5.20 p.m. even date Woo Sing Kung was in
the act of loading two cases of pirate cigarettes, kerosene, can-
dles and soap on a boat in the Soochow Creek near North Chekiang
Road Bridge, when he was approached by the aforementioned
Inspectors who demanded that he produce his tax receipt showing
that duty had been paid on the said cigarettes. He immediately
informed them that his company had purchased the cigarettes from
the Woo Fong (华丰) Cigarette Shop, No. 584 Foochow Road, and
were dispatching them to Hangchow together with other goods. He
also informed them that the cigarettes etc. would be sold on
arrival, and that rice would be purchased with the proceeds.

The Inspectors, however, not being satisfied, stated they
would have to take the cigarettes to their Head Office at No.
230 Kiukiang Road. They then attempted to remove the cigarettes
to another boat, whereupon, Woo Sing Kung informed the above
mentioned constables.

（左侧页边批注及印章：）
[印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 21 FEB 1938]
des B.
DBR.
S.I. 2/2
C.
[手写签名]

虹口西区巡捕房，
报告
日期：1938年2月20日。
事由：统税局成员非法行事。
呈报人：____ 库克（Cook） 转呈人：[签名]

先生：

1938年2月20日下午__时，警长24__号报告称，他逮捕了两名中国人，姓名如下：
(1) 李__（Lee Tuh），年龄__岁，松江籍，统税局第4号稽查员，以及
(2) 许坤__（Lee Kwen Jung），48岁，上海籍，统税局第9号稽查员，
他两次均在浙江北路附近将二人逮捕。此次逮捕是因天津路__弄__号华众__米店（Woo Chung Chu Pyi）的店员伍星根（Woo Sing Kung）举报，称此二人阻止他在苏州河上将两箱香烟装船。

经第311号华籍探员及本人随后的调查，查明当日约下午5时20分，伍星根正在浙江北路桥附近的苏州河上一艘船上装载两箱私制香烟、煤油、蜡烛和肥皂。上述稽查员上前要求他出示已就所述香烟缴纳税款的完税凭证。伍星根立即告知他们，其公司是从福州路584号华丰（Woo Fong）烟行购买的这些香烟，并正将其与其他货物一起发往杭州。他还告知他们，香烟等货物抵达后将被出售，所得款项将用于购买大米。

然而，稽查员对此并不满意，称必须将香烟带至九江路230号的总局。随后他们试图将香烟转移到另一艘船上，此时，伍星根向上述警员报了案。

（左侧页边批注及印章：）
[印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 1938年2月21日]
des B.
DBR.
S.I. 2/2
C.
[手写签名]
